subject: chemistry
title: Preparation of a soluble salt
apparatus: dilute acid; insoluble oxide/carbonate; beaker; spatula; filter funnel; evaporating basin; water bath/heater
independentVariable: mass of excess solid added or acid used
methodOverview: Warm dilute acid, add the insoluble solid in small portions until some remains, filter off excess solid, gently evaporate filtrate to concentrate, cool to crystallise, filter and dry crystals.
accuracyReliability: Add solid until excess remains; avoid boiling dry; rinse crystals with a little cold distilled water; dry to constant mass.
safety: Wear eye protection; acids are irritants; heat gently; take care with hot apparatus.
scientificRationale: Excess insoluble solid ensures all acid is neutralised; filtration removes excess reactant; cooling a concentrated solution forms crystals.
expectedPattern: Correct method produces pure salt solution followed by crystals; excessive heating can reduce yield or decompose product.
dataGraphFocus: Use mass/yield data and observations; distinguish soluble product in filtrate from insoluble excess residue.
commonError: Product is lost during transfers, filtration or because some remains dissolved.
improvement: Use quantitative transfer/rinsing, minimise solvent, cool fully, filter efficiently and dry to constant mass.

subject: chemistry
title: Acid–alkali titration
apparatus: burette; pipette and filler; conical flask; indicator; white tile; acid; alkali
controlVariables: aliquot volume; concentrations; indicator amount; technique
methodOverview: Rinse and fill burette with titrant, rinse pipette with analyte and transfer a fixed volume to a conical flask, add a few drops of indicator, perform a rough titration, then repeat dropwise near the endpoint until concordant titres are obtained.
accuracyReliability: Read burette at eye level to 2 decimal places, remove funnel, ensure jet is filled, swirl, use a white tile and average concordant titres only.
safety: Wear eye protection; use a pipette filler; acids and alkalis may be corrosive/irritant.
scientificRationale: Rinsing with the solution prevents dilution; only a few drops of indicator minimises its effect; a conical flask allows swirling without loss.
expectedPattern: Concordant titres are close together; the endpoint is a persistent indicator colour change, not necessarily pH 7.
dataGraphFocus: Present initial/final burette readings and titres; identify rough and concordant results; calculate a mean without the rough value.
commonError: Overshooting the endpoint makes titre too large and calculated unknown concentration inaccurate.
improvement: Add titrant dropwise near endpoint, wash flask sides with distilled water and repeat to obtain concordant titres.

subject: chemistry
title: Electrolysis of aqueous solutions
apparatus: electrolyte; inert electrodes; power supply; leads; test tubes; splints; indicator paper
dependentVariable: products at anode and cathode; observations
controlVariables: voltage/current; electrode area/distance; time; solution volume
methodOverview: Set up inert electrodes in an aqueous ionic solution without touching, connect to DC supply, collect gases or observe deposits, and test products safely. Record electrode polarity and observations.
accuracyReliability: Clean equal electrodes, fixed spacing/immersion, constant current/time, collect sufficient gas and use fresh test reagents.
safety: Wear eye protection; use low-voltage DC; gases may be flammable/toxic; test small volumes away from the cell.
scientificRationale: Ions move to oppositely charged electrodes; reduction occurs at cathode and oxidation at anode; products depend on ion reactivity and solution composition.
expectedPattern: At the cathode, hydrogen forms unless a less reactive metal ion is discharged; at the anode, halogen or oxygen may form.
dataGraphFocus: Use observations plus gas tests; write half-equations for Higher Tier and distinguish electrode products.
commonError: Gas escapes before collection or electrodes are not equally immersed.
improvement: Use gas-tight collection, fixed electrode area/depth, constant current, repeat and clean electrodes before weighing.

subject: chemistry
title: Temperature changes
apparatus: insulated cup; lid; thermometer/probe; measuring cylinder; reactant solutions/solids; balance; stirrer
controlVariables: total volume; starting temperature; insulation; stirring; measurement timing
methodOverview: Measure reactants, record initial temperature, mix in an insulated cup, stir and record temperature at short intervals until a maximum or minimum is reached. Repeat changed conditions one at a time.
accuracyReliability: Use lid and insulation, temperature probe/data logger, equal starting temperatures, rapid transfer and extrapolate a cooling curve where appropriate.
safety: Wear eye protection; acids/alkalis may irritate; avoid excessive concentrations; handle hot/cold mixtures carefully.
scientificRationale: Insulation and lid reduce energy transfer to surroundings; stirring distributes energy; frequent readings capture the true peak.
expectedPattern: Exothermic reactions raise temperature; endothermic reactions lower it. Greater reacting amount may increase ΔT if heat capacity is controlled.
dataGraphFocus: Plot temperature against time; infer corrected peak by extrapolation and compare ΔT fairly.
commonError: Energy transfers to cup, thermometer and surroundings, reducing measured temperature change.
improvement: Improve insulation/lid, use a lower-heat-capacity container, data logging and cooling-curve extrapolation.

subject: chemistry
title: Rates of reaction
topic: Rate and Extent of Chemical Change
apparatus: conical flask; gas syringe; balance; stopwatch; acid; marble chips; sodium thiosulfate; cross; measuring cylinders
dependentVariable: gas volume/mass loss/turbidity time and rate
controlVariables: temperature; reactant amounts; apparatus; total volume; endpoint
methodOverview: Use either gas collection/mass loss for acid–carbonate or disappearance of a cross for thiosulfate. Change one factor, start timing on mixing, record at fixed intervals or a defined endpoint, repeat and compare rates.
accuracyReliability: Check gas-tightness, use a gas syringe, fixed endpoint/observer or colorimeter, precise volumes, constant temperature and repeats.
safety: Wear eye protection; acids irritate; sulfur dioxide from thiosulfate should be produced on small scale in ventilation.
scientificRationale: Higher concentration or surface area increases collision frequency; higher temperature increases collision frequency and fraction above activation energy.
expectedPattern: Steeper initial gradient or shorter time means faster rate; curves plateau when limiting reactant is used up.
dataGraphFocus: Plot product quantity against time, calculate gradient over a stated interval and distinguish initial from mean rate.
commonError: Gas may escape while the bung is fitted, reducing early readings.
improvement: Use a dropping funnel/syringe through the bung, practise coordinated start, data logger or mass-loss method, and repeat.

subject: chemistry
title: Paper chromatography
apparatus: chromatography paper; pencil; ruler; capillary tubes; solvent; beaker with lid; reference dyes
dependentVariable: number/position of spots and Rf values
controlVariables: baseline height; solvent depth; paper; temperature; spot size
methodOverview: Draw a pencil baseline, place small concentrated spots, stand paper in solvent below the baseline, cover, allow solvent to rise, remove before the top, mark solvent front immediately, dry and calculate Rf.
accuracyReliability: Use pencil, small spots, capillary tubes, lid and repeated reference standards; measure from baseline to spot centre.
safety: Wear eye protection; some solvents are flammable/irritant; use ventilation and no flames.
scientificRationale: Pencil is insoluble; baseline must be above solvent; lid reduces evaporation; components separate because of different affinities for mobile and stationary phases.
expectedPattern: A pure substance gives one spot in that solvent; a mixture may give several. Identical Rf under the same conditions supports, but does not prove, identity.
dataGraphFocus: Record spot distances and solvent-front distance; calculate Rf and compare only under identical conditions.
commonError: A large wet starting spot causes streaking and overlapping components.
improvement: Apply smaller spots, dry between applications, use a different solvent or longer paper and repeat.

subject: chemistry
title: Identification of ions
apparatus: flame-test wire; Bunsen burner; sodium hydroxide; dilute nitric acid; silver nitrate; dilute hydrochloric acid; barium chloride; test tubes
controlVariables: reagent concentration/volume; clean apparatus; test order
methodOverview: Use clean flame tests for selected cations, sodium hydroxide precipitates for metal ions, acid then silver nitrate for halides, acid then barium chloride for sulfate, and dilute acid plus limewater for carbonate. Record observation before inference.
accuracyReliability: Clean flame-test wire until no colour; use fresh labelled reagents; split sample into portions; include known controls.
safety: Wear eye protection; acids/alkalis irritate; silver nitrate stains; barium compounds are harmful; use small quantities.
scientificRationale: Acidification removes interfering ions; separate sample portions avoid reagent contamination; clean wire prevents false flame colours.
expectedPattern: Li crimson, Na yellow, K lilac, Ca orange-red, Cu green; halides give white/cream/yellow AgX; sulfate gives white BaSO₄; carbonate releases CO₂.
dataGraphFocus: Use a decision sequence and distinguish observation from conclusion; ambiguous white precipitates require the correct reagent context.
commonError: Contaminated wire often gives sodium’s intense yellow flame and masks other colours.
improvement: Clean with acid and flame repeatedly, use separate wires and view through cobalt glass only if instructed/appropriate.

subject: chemistry
title: Water analysis and purification
apparatus: water samples; pH probe; balance; evaporating basin; filter; simple distillation apparatus; heat source
dependentVariable: pH, dissolved-solid mass, appearance and purity
controlVariables: sample volume; apparatus; heating; drying; calibration
methodOverview: Observe sample, measure pH, filter suspended solids, evaporate a measured portion to estimate dissolved solids, and use simple distillation to obtain pure water. Test before and after treatment.
accuracyReliability: Calibrate pH probe, measure accurate volume, dry residue to constant mass, use clean apparatus and prevent distillate contamination.
safety: Wear eye protection; heat gently; clamp apparatus; never seal distillation; samples may be biologically unsafe and should not be tasted.
scientificRationale: Filtration removes insoluble solids but not dissolved substances; evaporation reveals dissolved solids; distillation separates water by boiling and condensation.
expectedPattern: Distillate should contain much less dissolved solid and have pH near neutral, though these alone do not prove it is safe to drink.
dataGraphFocus: Compare before/after data and calculate dissolved-solid concentration; evaluate several purity measures.
commonError: Heating too strongly causes spitting and loss of dissolved solid.
improvement: Heat gently, use a larger basin, dry to constant mass and cool before weighing.
